subject: physics
question_text: An object projected with a velocity greater than or equal to 11.2 km s⁻¹ will not return to the earth. Explain the reason.

verification.note: Listed by the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (book p.26, Short Answer 4) and NOT by the Sri Chaitanya Fastrack — the union of the two books is the bank. The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.why: Naming the number is most of the answer: the question is really "what is special about 11.2 km/s?"
common_mistakes: Calling it the orbital velocity, which is 7.9 km/s.

recall.must_convey: That 11.2 kilometres per second is the escape velocity of the earth, root 2 g R.

steps.label: Why it does not return
lines: A body projected at exactly this speed has just
enough kinetic energy to do all the work needed
against the earth’s pull on the whole way out.

lines.text: The body never returns to the earth.

steps.why: Gravity never becomes exactly zero, but it falls off as 1/r² fast enough that a FINITE amount of energy is enough to get clear.
common_mistakes: Saying gravity stops acting beyond some height; it never stops, it only weakens.

recall.must_convey: That the body has enough kinetic energy to do all the work against gravity, with energy left over, so it never returns.
